# Moneo

Moneo is an open-source personal finance workspace you run on your own computer. Import statements or sync your bank, track accounts and wealth, plan spending, and ask questions about your money in chat or on a voice call. Financial figures always come from your own records; the AI explains them and proposes changes you accept.

It is a Next.js and TypeScript app. The backend (Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services) runs in Docker on your machine. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace, and everything stays on `127.0.0.1`.

## Run it

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22+ and [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS).

```sh
npm ci
npm run setup              # creates .env with fresh secrets, starts the database, applies migrations
npm run build && npm start # then open http://localhost:3000
```

`npm run setup` is safe to rerun. Run it again after every `git pull` to apply new migrations; your data and secrets are kept. For development, use `npm run dev` instead of build and start.

The database keeps running in Docker after you stop Moneo (`docker compose stop` stops it, `docker compose up -d` starts it again). Your data lives in Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`; `docker compose down` keeps them, `docker compose down -v` deletes them.

Everything listens on `127.0.0.1` only, so other devices on your network cannot open Moneo. Keep `.env` private: it holds the database password and the keys that sign the owner in.

## AI

Settings → **AI access** offers two equal options, and you choose which one pays:

- **ChatGPT plan**: click **Sign in with ChatGPT** and allow plan usage. Requests count toward your Go, Plus or Pro plan's limits.
- **OpenAI API key**: paste it under **OpenAI API key** and click **Save key**. Usage is billed to that key.

You can also save an **OpenRouter API key** there. Keys are checked with the provider before they are saved, stored encrypted in Moneo's database (they survive restarts and Reset all data), shown only by their last four characters, and can be replaced or removed at any time. You don't need to edit `.env`.

Voice calls and dictation need the OpenAI API key, because ChatGPT plan usage and OpenRouter don't support realtime audio. Models are chosen per agent under Settings → AI and your data; IDs with a `/` (for example `vendor/model`) go to OpenRouter. With only an OpenRouter key, the plain default IDs run on OpenRouter as `openai/<id>`.

Older installs that set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `.env` keep working; a key saved in the app takes precedence.

## Background jobs

While Moneo runs, it checks hourly for scheduled summaries, review recovery, bank sync and Scalable Capital sync. Each sync runs about once a day, and anything missed while the computer was off runs shortly after Moneo starts.

## Scalable Capital (optional)

First turn on access in Scalable on the web under Profile → Security → Agentic Investing (read-only is enough). Then **Connect Scalable Capital** (on Import or in Settings) opens Scalable's login (with 2FA in the Scalable app). Moneo then reads your holdings, totals and cash daily as wealth records, and shows the portfolio on Accounts. It uses Scalable's official read-only MCP server and needs no keys.

## Connect your bank (optional)

Moneo can sync booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). Its restricted mode is free for personal use and covers the accounts you link yourself. Each sync is written as an ordinary import, so it shows in import history and can be reviewed and undone.

1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create an application in the **Production** environment. A new production app runs in restricted mode: free, and limited to the accounts you link yourself.
2. Fill in the application form:
   - Redirect URL: `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback`
   - Privacy policy URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/privacy.html`
   - Terms of service URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/terms.html`
3. Let the control panel generate the key pair and keep the downloaded private key (`<application-id>.pem`).
4. In the control panel, link your own accounts to the application. Only linked accounts can be synced.
5. In Moneo, open **Import → Connected banks**, paste the application ID, paste the private key or upload the `.pem` file, and click **Save and check**. Moneo checks them with Enable Banking and stores them encrypted; **Replace** and **Remove** are next to the bank picker. (An existing `ENABLE_BANKING_APP_ID` and `ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY` in `.env` keep working until you save new ones here.)
6. Use **Import → Connected banks → Choose a bank → Connect bank**. If Enable Banking says it rejected the return address, add the Redirect URL from step 2 to your application and try again.

Consent usually lasts up to 180 days, depending on the bank, and a reconnect banner appears 7 days before it ends. PSD2 allows about 4 background fetches a day per bank; Moneo syncs about once a day, and **Sync now** runs with you present, so it doesn't count. Pending transactions are not synced.

Enable Banking only accepts `https://` return addresses, so after you approve access the bank sends you to `https://localhost:3443`. Moneo answers there with a certificate `npm run setup` made and trusted on this computer only (using [mkcert](https://github.com/FiloSottile/mkcert); the first run may ask you to allow it), and passes you straight back to Moneo.

## Checks

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | Unit tests |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm run build` | Production build |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Playwright browser tests (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md)) |

Browser tests use a separate QA user, never the owner's workspace: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` creates it and saves its session, and `--reset` empties its workspace.

Most of this is already built. It landed in the last merge (`cb8e9fd9`, "in-app service keys"). Here's what exists, what can't leave `.env`, and what I'd still change.

## Already in the app

| Key | Where you enter it now | `.env` still needed? |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI API key | Settings → AI access | No (the `.env` value is only a fallback) |
| ChatGPT sign-in | Settings → AI access | No |
| OpenRouter API key | Settings → AI access | No (fallback only) |
| Enable Banking App ID and private key | Import → Connected banks, and Settings → Connected banks | No (fallback only) |
| Scalable Capital | Connect button with Scalable's login, no keys | No |
| AI models for each agent | Settings → AI and your data | No |

Keys are checked with the provider before they're saved. They're stored encrypted in the database and shown only by their last 4 characters, and you can replace or remove them in the app.

## What has to stay in `.env`

The rest of `.env` is the app's startup config. The app needs it before it can even connect to the database, so it can't be stored in the database:

- **`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_*`**: how the app reaches and signs in to its own database.
- **`MONEO_OWNER_EMAIL` / `PASSWORD`**: the automatic owner sign-in.
- **`BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`**: the key that encrypts all the saved keys. If it were stored in the database next to them, the encryption would protect nothing.
- **`CRON_SECRET`**: protects the background job routes.

A new user never types any of these. `npm run setup` generates them all. So the file has to exist on disk, but nobody needs to open it. Moving it to another file such as `.data/config.json` would only rename it, so I'd keep `.env` and stop presenting it as something to fill in.

## Gaps for a new user (README and setup)

1. **No "what next" after setup.** The README's Run section ends at "open localhost:3000" and never says "now go to Settings → AI access and add a key or sign in with ChatGPT". I'd add a short **First run** checklist: AI (required for chat) → bank (optional) → Scalable (optional).
2. **`.env.example` still lists `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `ENABLE_BANKING_*` near the top.** A newcomer will think they need to fill them in. I'd move them to a clearly marked "legacy overrides, leave empty" block at the bottom, or drop them from the example entirely while the code keeps reading them.
3. **The setup output doesn't point anywhere.** `npm run setup` could finish by printing "Open http://localhost:3000 → Settings → AI access to add your key."
4. **Keys are split across two places.** AI keys are under "AI access" and bank keys under "Connected banks". If you want literally one "Keys and connections" section in Settings, I can group them. Otherwise the current split is fine; the main fix is a pointer.
5. **Small things worth checking:** the first run on Windows may show a mkcert trust prompt (the README mentions it, only under the bank section), and Docker Desktop must be running before setup. Nothing in the README says so.

## Questions before I change anything

- Should **`.env.example` drop the legacy key lines entirely**, or keep them marked as overrides? I'd keep them, moved to the bottom.
- Do you want a **single "Keys and connections" section** in Settings, or keep AI access and Connected banks separate and just fix the README and setup messages? I'd fix the docs and messages first; that's a small change.
- Should I also do a fresh-install test (new clone, new Docker project name, not your volumes) to find setup problems I can't see from reading? It won't touch your workspace.

Yes the .env.example should drop the legacy lines entirely. Yes I want the single keys and connection section in settings. Also fix the readme and setup message. Sure do it but it should not require me to do something.

Another thing is I think we should add a skill or something that we can give the user so that they can use the skill to navigate through the install and setup process using an agent like Claude Code or Codex on their own as well. They took me to open banking. It did not ask me but if you're saying that it did not because it got it from me, then it's fine. Yes do have something like that in one place where all the env things are there.

Fix all of those things, delete the backlog file itself, and put those things in the GitHub issues. That's another thing you should do. Check a fresh install, find all the problems that it has, and then ask for that and make changes to it. Honestly the readme should be in simple clear words, step by step: do this, do this, do this. Do that after doing the fresh install test and then see what all things a new user will have to find and all of that, XYZ.

# Backlog

## In-app service keys: follow-ups
Keys for OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking are entered in the app (Settings → AI access, Import → Connected banks) and sealed in `service_keys`.
- Optional one-click "Move to the app" that copies a key still in `.env` into the database; today the `.env` value is used until a key is saved in the app, and nothing is removed from `.env`.

- `scripts/voice-call-check.mjs` still reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment.
- Keys are cached for 5 seconds per process; a second server process sees a change within that time.

## Self-hosted: phone access from anywhere
Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).
- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).
- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.

## Multi-currency on Home
Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).

- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.

Playwright tests run against the app on http://localhost:3000. The config starts it (`npm run dev`, or the production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless a server is already running there.

1. Start the backend: `npm run setup`.

## Running

# Moneo

Moneo is an open-source personal finance app that runs on your own computer. Import bank statements or sync your bank, track accounts and wealth, plan spending, and ask questions about your money in chat or on a voice call. Figures always come from your own records; the AI explains them and suggests changes that you accept.

Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital).

## Install

**Prefer help?** Open this folder in an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex and say "set up Moneo". It follows the `moneo-setup` skill in this repository and walks you through every step below.

### 1. Install the tools

- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) version 22 or newer
- [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (on Linux, Docker Engine with Compose)

Start Docker Desktop and wait until it says it is running.

### 2. Download Moneo

```sh
git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
```

### 3. Run the setup

```sh
npm run setup
```

This creates the database in Docker, makes all the passwords and secrets Moneo needs, and saves them in a file called `.env`. The first run downloads about 1 GB and takes a few minutes. On Windows a security prompt may ask to install a local certificate: click **Yes** (it is only used for bank connections and only trusted on this computer).

You never need to open or edit `.env`. Keep it private and don't delete it.

### 4. Start Moneo

```sh
npm run build
npm start
```

The build takes a few minutes the first time. Then open **http://localhost:3000**.

### 5. Turn on the AI

Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and choose one:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** to use your ChatGPT Go, Plus or Pro plan, or
- **Paste an OpenAI API key** ([create one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)) and click **Save key**. Usage is billed to that key.

Voice calls and dictation need the OpenAI API key. An OpenRouter key is optional (for other models).

### 6. Add your money

- **Import** a CSV or Excel export from your bank, or
- connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below).

That's it.

## Everyday use

- **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running).
- **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it.
- **Update Moneo:**
  ```sh
  git pull
  npm ci
  npm run setup
  npm run build
  npm start
  ```
  Your data and secrets are kept.

While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo.

## Keys and connections

Every key and outside service is set up in the app under **Settings → Keys and connections**. Keys are checked with the provider before they are saved, stored encrypted in your database, shown only by their last four characters, and can be replaced or removed at any time. The same section shows that the secrets made by `npm run setup` are in place.

### Connect your bank (optional)

Moneo syncs booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). It is free for personal use. Each sync is an ordinary import that you can review and undo.

1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create an application in the **Production** environment.
2. Fill in the application form:
   - Redirect URL: `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback`
   - Privacy policy URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/privacy.html`
   - Terms of service URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/terms.html`
3. Let the control panel make the key pair, and keep the downloaded private key file (`<application-id>.pem`).
4. In the control panel, link your own bank accounts to the application. Only linked accounts can be synced.
5. In Moneo, go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks** (also on the Import page). Paste the application ID, paste the private key or upload the `.pem` file, and click **Save and check**.
6. Click **Choose a bank**, pick yours, click **Connect bank** and approve access at your bank.

Bank consent usually lasts up to 180 days; Moneo shows a reconnect banner 7 days before it ends. Pending transactions are not synced. If Enable Banking says it rejected the return address, add the Redirect URL from step 2 to your application and try again.

### Connect Scalable Capital (optional)

1. In Scalable on the web, go to **Profile → Security → Agentic Investing** and turn on access (read-only is enough).
2. In Moneo, click **Connect Scalable Capital** under **Settings → Keys and connections** (also on the Import page) and log in to Scalable (with 2FA in the Scalable app).

Moneo then reads your holdings, totals and cash every day and shows the portfolio on Accounts. No keys are needed.

## Good to know

- Moneo only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other devices on your network can't open it.
- Your data lives in the Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`. `docker compose down` keeps them; **`docker compose down -v` deletes all your data**.
- If ports 54321 or 54322 are already in use, add `API_PORT=` and `DB_PORT=` with free ports to `.env` and run `npm run setup` again.

## Development

Use `npm run dev` instead of build and start. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for how the project works.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | Unit tests |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm run build` | Production build |
| `npm run test:e2e` | Playwright browser tests (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md)) |

Browser tests use a separate QA user, never the owner's workspace: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` creates it and saves its session, and `--reset` empties its workspace.

# Set up Moneo

You are helping a person, often not a developer, run Moneo on their own computer. Do the commands yourself, explain each step in one plain sentence, and only ask them for things only they can do (install an app, click in a browser, paste a key into Moneo). The README's **Install** section is the same flow written for people.

## Rules

- Never ask the person to paste API keys, bank keys or passwords into this chat. Keys go into Moneo's own page: **Settings → Keys and connections**.
- Never edit `.env` by hand, except `API_PORT` / `DB_PORT` for a port clash. `npm run setup` writes everything else.
- Never change `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`, never delete `.env`, and never run `docker compose down -v` or delete the `moneo_*` Docker volumes. That is the person's financial data.
- Only stop processes you started.

## Steps

1. **Check the tools.** Run `git --version`, `node --version` (needs 22 or newer) and `docker info`.
   - Missing Git, Node or Docker: give the download link (git-scm.com/downloads, nodejs.org, docs.docker.com/get-docker) and wait for them to install it.
   - `docker info` fails: Docker Desktop is not running. Ask them to start it and wait until it says it is running.
2. **Get the code.** If you are not already in a Moneo checkout (`package.json` with `"name": "moneo"`), run `git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git` and `cd Moneo`. Then `npm ci`.
3. **Run the setup:** `npm run setup`. It creates `.env` with fresh secrets, starts the database in Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner and makes a local HTTPS certificate. The first run downloads about 1 GB. On Windows, tell them a "Security Warning" about installing a certificate may appear and to click **Yes**. It is safe to rerun.
4. **Start Moneo:** `npm run build`, then `npm start` (keep it running; use a background terminal if you can). Open http://localhost:3000.
5. **Turn on the AI.** Ask them to open **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and either click **Sign in with ChatGPT** (Go, Plus or Pro plan) or paste an OpenAI API key from https://platform.openai.com/api-keys and click **Save key**. Voice calls need the API key.
6. **Optional: bank.** Follow the README section "Connect your bank". The person creates an Enable Banking application (Production) with redirect URL `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback`, links their own accounts there, and pastes the App ID and `.pem` key into **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks**.
7. **Optional: Scalable Capital.** They turn on Agentic Investing in Scalable (Profile → Security), then click **Connect Scalable Capital** in the same Settings section.
8. **Finish** by telling them how to start Moneo next time (`npm start` with Docker running) and how to update (`git pull`, `npm ci`, `npm run setup`, `npm run build`, `npm start`).

## When something goes wrong

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `docker` not found, or "cannot connect to the Docker daemon" | Install or start Docker Desktop, then rerun `npm run setup`. |
| "port is already allocated" for 54321 or 54322 | Add `API_PORT=55421` and `DB_PORT=55422` (any free ports) to `.env` and rerun `npm run setup`. |
| Port 3000 in use | Something else runs there. Stop it, or `npm start -- -p 3001` and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3001` in `.env`, then rerun setup and rebuild. |
| ".env points at a hosted Supabase" | That `.env` belongs to another setup. Rename it (don't delete it) and rerun `npm run setup`. |
| "Could not create the local HTTPS certificate" | Only bank connections need it. Rerun `npm run setup` and accept the certificate prompt. |
| Chat says "No AI is set up yet" | Step 5. |
| Bank says the return address was rejected | Add `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` as a redirect URL in the Enable Banking application. |
| The page shows a database error after `git pull` | Run `npm run setup` (applies new migrations), then `npm run build` and `npm start`. |

Everything you asked for is done and committed in 4 steps on `t3/settings-credentials-readme-setup`. Nothing is pushed and no PR is open. Unit tests, lint, build and the new browser test pass. One database test timed out while the machine was busy and passed when I re-ran it alone.

## Changes

- **Settings → Keys and connections:** one section now holds AI access (ChatGPT, OpenAI and OpenRouter keys), Connected banks (the Enable Banking ID and key), Scalable Capital, and a new "Set up automatically" list. That list shows that the database, owner sign-in, encryption key and background-job secret from `npm run setup` are in place, but never shows their values. I checked it on desktop and on a phone-sized screen in dark mode; I fixed one text-wrapping problem on the phone. The chat's guide to the app now points there too.
- **`.env.example`:** the OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking key lines are gone, and it now opens with "You don't need to edit this file". Your own `.env` keeps working because the app still reads those values as a fallback.
- **Setup messages:**
  - If Docker isn't installed or isn't running, setup now says so in plain words. Before, it crashed with a stack trace.
  - It warns that the first run downloads a few GB.
  - It ends with numbered next steps: start Moneo, open the page, add AI under Keys and connections.
- **README:** rewritten as six plain steps:
  1. Install Git, Node and Docker.
  2. Download Moneo (`git clone`, which the old README never mentioned).
  3. Run setup.
  4. Start Moneo.
  5. Turn on the AI.
  6. Add your money.

  After that come everyday use (start, stop, update), the bank and Scalable steps, and good-to-know notes. I also fixed a wrong pointer: the Scalable portfolio is on Wealth, not Accounts.
- **Setup skill:** in [.agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-6ab236ab\.agents\skills\moneo-setup\SKILL.md). Codex reads it from there, and `.claude/skills/moneo-setup` points Claude Code to the same file. It walks the agent through the setup, never asks for keys in the chat, protects `.env` and the Docker volumes, and includes a troubleshooting table.
- **BACKLOG.md** is deleted. Its items are now GitHub issues #148–#158, and AGENTS.md now says deferred work goes in issues.

## Fresh install test

I ran a clean clone under a separate Docker project with its own ports, then deleted it. Your `moneo_*` volumes were never touched, and you didn't have to do anything. The basics worked: install took 3 minutes, setup 25 seconds (the Docker images were already on this machine), the build 4.5 minutes, and with no AI set up, chat shows a clear "No AI is set up yet" message.

Problems it found:

| Problem | Status |
|---|---|
| README never said how to download the code | Fixed |
| Setup crashed with a stack trace when Docker wasn't running | Fixed |
| No "what next" after setup | Fixed |
| The first download is a few GB (about 3.3 GB of images on disk), not mentioned anywhere | Fixed (README and setup) |
| Home doesn't tell a new user to turn on AI, and still shows "Run agent team" | Open, see question 1 |
| A key already set in the computer's environment is used without saying so | Open, see question 2 |
| `docker-compose.yml` fixes the project name to `moneo`, so a second copy of Moneo on the same computer would share (and break) the first one's database | Open, see question 3 |

The second problem showed up because your shell has a global `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, so the "fresh" app looked like AI was already set up. One test message went to OpenRouter with that key before I noticed; it was rejected for lack of credits, so it cost nothing.

## Questions

1. Should Home show "Turn on AI → Settings" as the first step and hide or disable "Run agent team" until AI is set up?
2. Should Settings label a key that comes from the environment rather than the app (as it already does for the Enable Banking key)?
3. Should I make the project name follow the folder name, or add a warning instead? Changing the name would affect your existing install, so I'd keep `moneo` as the default.
4. Should I open a PR?
